description: Somo alumnos del primer año de la carrera de Analilsis de sistema y Ingieneria en Informatica, nos enfocares en construir un sistema real y funcional con alto impacto ambiental, combinando código robusto, flujos automatizados y ciencia agrícola para ayudar a los agricultores a adaptarse al cambio climático.
summary: Field Shift is a Laravel web platform that translates NASA satellite and meteorological data into useful information for small and medium-scale farmers in regions like Paraguay, affected by climate change, soil degradation, and water scarcity. The system combines two types of intelligence: deterministic rule-based logic for alerts, rainfall/temperature risk detection, and crop-rotation ranking (reproducible results without an LLM), and LLMs for conversational agronomy advice and the narrative of each alert. It benefits local farmers (alerts, rotation plans, and practical advice), agroecological consultants (field comparison, satellite imagery, and NASA granules), and the environment (regenerative practices, soil health, and carbon sequestration). It uses data from NASA POWER (temperature, rainfall, humidity, wind, solar radiation), GPM IMERG (daily precipitation and derived metrics), SMAP (soil moisture), Landsat, MODIS, ECOSTRESS, SRTM, and GIBS/Worldview. Fields are resolved by latitude/longitude with a ±0.05° tolerance. NDVI is implemented but not yet integrated into the scheduler, so values remain NULL until the pipeline is completed.
details:
What does it do or how does it work? Field Shift is a web platform that acts as a smart translator between Earth observation satellite data and daily fieldwork. It fetches raw NASA data (precipitation, soil moisture, surface temperature) via Laravel background jobs, processes it, and stores it directly in JSON format in MariaDB. An AI assistant then reads this data and converts it into conversational agronomic recommendations.

What are its benefits? It simplifies complex scientific information so any farmer can use it without needing to be a data science expert. It provides early warnings for drought or heavy rain risks, generates crop rotation plans to optimize soil health, and accurately tracks reforestation initiatives.

What is the project's expected impact? The main impact is empowering local farmers to face climate change unpredictability through regenerative agriculture. By basing decisions on real-time scientific data, the system aims to prevent crop loss, reduce soil degradation, optimize water usage, and increase farm resilience.

What tools, programming languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Languages & Frameworks: PHP 8.3 (Laravel) for microservices architecture and API processing, alongside Bootstrap 5 for the frontend.
  • Database: MariaDB, optimized for storing and querying raw JSON data.
  • NASA APIs: POWER (weather data), GPM (precipitation), SMAP (soil moisture), Landsat and MODIS (vegetation indices like NDVI), ECOSTRESS, and SRTM.
  • AI: Gemini API (v1beta endpoint) for fast cloud processing, with an architecture ready for local LLM execution via Ollama.

How is your project creative? Its creativity lies in not just being a metrics dashboard. Instead of showing complex moisture or temperature charts that the user must decipher, the project uses AI to cross-reference spatial telemetry with agroecological rules. The system delivers direct, human responses, such as: "Based on SMAP soil moisture data from the last 3 days, wait until Thursday to plant your cover crops."

What factors did your team consider?

  • Multidisciplinary approach: We bridged the knowledge gap by uniting software developers with UEP agroecology students, ensuring the code solved a real biological problem.
  • Performance & Technical limits: We implemented Laravel Jobs to handle NASA API rate limits without crashing the server.
  • Architectural efficiency: We opted against using a heavy vector database, choosing instead to process JSON data directly from MariaDB into AI prompts, achieving a much faster and viable prototype for resource-constrained environments.
